'''''Ammonitritor''''' ({{lit|[[ammonite]] grinder}}) is an [[extinct]] genus of early [[ichthyosauriform]] in the family [[Omphalosauridae]], known from the [[Early Triassic]] ([[Olenekian]] age) [[Vikinghøgda Formation]] of Norway. The genus contains a [[Monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Ammonitritor scientiacivium''''', known from a nearly complete skull and partial vertebral column. This specimen is the first described skull of an omphalosaurid to be preserved in three dimensions, contrasting with the flattened skulls of other members of this clade.

== Discovery and naming ==

The ''Ammonitritor'' fossil material was discovered by Felix Saludes during a 2010 expedition led by Luc Ebbo to outcrops of the [[Vikinghøgda Formation]] (Vendomdalen Member). These rock layers—part of the ''[[Grippia]]'' Niveau ({{lit|''Grippia'' level}})—are located on Vikinghøgda mountain's northwest slope, a site near the [[Sassendalen]] glacial valley on [[Spitsbergen]] island of Svalbard, Norway.<ref name="Ammonitritor" />

The specimen was preserved within a [[calcareous]] [[septarian concretion]] that had broken into several pieces. Once collected, the fragments were reassembled, and Ebbo [[Fossil preparation|prepared]] the concretion in 2020. Four years later, casts of the specimen were produced and eventually sent to museums in Sweden, Switzerland, China, and the United States. The original specimen is now housed in Ebbo's ''Paléogalerie'' in [[Salignac, Alpes-de-Haute-Provence|Salignac]], France, under specimen number PGE LE 2024.0.264. It consists of a nearly complete skull and mandible preserved alongside several vertebrae from the neck and possibly the trunk. Notably, while the skull is partially disarticulated and some elements (braincase and palate) are missing, the parts that are present are preserved three-dimensionally. This makes it the first omphalosaurid specimen known from a 3D skull, contrasting with those of all other omphalosaurids, which are crushed, flattened, or incomplete to some extent.<ref name="Ammonitritor" />

In 2026, P. Martin Sander, Luc Ebbo, and colleagues [[Species description|described]] ''Ammonitritor scientiacivium'' as a new genus and species of omphalosaurid ichthyosauriform based on these fossil remains, designating PGE LE 2024.0.264 as the [[holotype]] specimen. The [[Genus|generic name]], ''Ammonitritor'', combines {{gloss|[[ammonite]]}} with the [[Latin]] {{lang|la|[[:wikt:tritus|tritor]]}}, meaning {{gloss|grinder}}, alluding to the taxon's possible diet and means of feeding. The [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]], ''scientiacivium'', is derived from the Latin words {{lang|la|[[:wikt:scientia|scientia]]}} ({{gloss|science}}) and {{lang|la|[[:wikt:civis#Latin|civis]]}} ({{gloss|citizen}}), honoring the contributions of [[citizen scientist]]s to paleontology, including those that resulted in the discovery and description of this species.<ref name="Ammonitritor" />

== Classification ==
To test the affinities and relationships of ''Ammonitritor'', Sander et al. (2026) included it in an updated version of the [[phylogenetic]] matrix of Fang et al. (2024).<ref name="Fang2024" /> Their best-resolved [[Maximum parsimony|parsimony]] tree placed ''Ammonitritor'' as a member of the [[ichthyosauriform]] family [[Omphalosauridae]], diverging after ''[[Cartorhynchus]]'' but before ''[[Sclerocormus]]'' and ''[[Omphalosaurus]]'' spp. These results are displayed in the [[cladogram]] below:<ref name="Ammonitritor" />
